A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MARVAL research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation results, inference timings, CFG and sampling-step ablations, and evaluations before and after RL refinement.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative and qualitative text-to-image results using DC-AR.

M1.justification: The GSIM objective, auxiliary network, Pseudo-Huber loss and separate reward-based refinement procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.5 applies this framework to DC-AR without documenting a new algorithmic component or procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditional ImageNet generation. v2 additionally evaluates open-ended text-to-image generation using JourneyDB prompts, substantially extending coverage to richer textual conditions and another generation task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds DC-AR-512 with 20-step DDIM as a comparator against distilled-and-refined DC-AR. The existing ImageNet comparator lineup is retained.

E3.justification: The added text-to-image evaluation uses 50,000 randomly sampled JourneyDB test prompts and compares 20-step DDIM against one-step generation plus RL using ImageReward. Existing ImageNet sampling, metrics and experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 adds a qualitative DC-AR case comparison, discussed in terms of facial detail and prompt adherence. Existing CFG, sampling-step and ImageNet RL ablations are unchanged. The supplementary prompt gallery does not constitute a controlled prompt-length robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The added experiment continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds a limited quantitative comparison: ImageReward is 0.5876 for DC-AR-512 with 20-step DDIM and 0.6903 for distilled DC-AR plus RL, alongside new qualitative samples. These are newly reported text-to-image results; the existing ImageNet numbers and image examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, Gradient Equivalent Theorem, score-projection identity and supplementary proof remain unchanged. Equation reflow and citation renumbering do not alter their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and main conclusion retain the same contributions: variational distillation for fast MAR inference and practical preference-based refinement. The headline FID and acceleration claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes the substantive limitations discussion about RL memory demands, restricted batch sizes, worsening scaling costs and possible mitigations. It also replaces prospective text-to-image applicability with affirmative interpretations of preserved quality and improved alignment in Section 4.5, substantially changing the qualifications around practical applicability.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and explicit prompts for new qualitative examples. Existing MARVAL hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures are retained. No dedicated DC-AR training configuration is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to DC-AR and JourneyDB, while removing the CLIPScore, FID and ImageReward references accompanying the deleted metrics paragraph. The broader diffusion, distillation and preference-alignment positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the experimental setup, removes its metrics paragraph and the limitations subsection, adds Section 4.5, and expands the supplementary results introduction. There is also an affiliation edit. Most existing prose and the overall organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The architecture table becomes prose with its values preserved. Retained tables are renumbered, and v2 adds text-to-image Table 4, main Figure 5 and supplementary Figure 3. Existing figures are retained, with localized layout changes.

improvement.justification: The JourneyDB/DC-AR experiment supplies empirical support for applicability that v1 left as future work. However, its evidence is limited to one reward metric and examples, without a distillation-only control or dedicated training details, while v2 removes important memory and scaling limitations. The added validation and reduced qualification create a tradeoff whose net effect on overall quality is uncertain.
